correspondence.component_scope: Initial feeder west of Caetés and northern Riacho Seco corridor
correspondence.finding: The Caetés original accounts for the selected short headward approach west of the town in the Pedra Grande/Riacho Seco setting, its southwesterly passage toward Barriguda and its southeastern bend. The map labels Riacho Seco along the connected corridor. The exact spring and a separate hydronym for the initial tip are not assigned; its geographic connection is visible rather than inferred from a basin label.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Umbuzeiro–Macambira–Miracica headward continuation
correspondence.finding: Overlapping Caetés and Paranatama originals show the stream bending southeast at Umbuzeiro, crossing BR-423 and continuing south by Macambira toward the Miracica setting. This is the selected western headwater, separate from the Mundaú/Canhoto headward system farther east.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: West of Brejão through Terezinha toward Sítio Grande
correspondence.finding: The Brejão original follows the western stream through the Grota do Riacho Seco/Mamoeiro setting, south past the western side of Brejão, then southeast below Terezinha toward Sítio Grande. Arapiraca overlaps the continuation and distinguishes the eastern Riacho Caracol inflow. Açude Público Garanhuns is on a separate northeastern watercourse and is not a selected reservoir passage.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Lagoa do Ouro western boundary and Seco–Paraíba transition
correspondence.finding: The Lagoa do Ouro original shows the selected southern continuation along the western municipal boundary, with Riacho Seco labeled above and Rio Paraíba below the western inflow in the Bom Conselho boundary setting. The selected corridor proceeds beside the western flank of Serra dos Carneiros/Serra do Catolé. The name-transition point is not fixed to a model vertex. Eastern Cocal, Cavaleiro and Piapai branches are separate from the selected headward choice. The Arapiraca original supplies continuous overlapping geographic coverage to Quebrangulo.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Quebrangulo and eastward middle river
correspondence.finding: The Arapiraca original follows the southward river into Quebrangulo and its turn east through Paulo Jacinto, the Anel vicinity, Viçosa and Cajueiro. It directly distinguishes the western Bálsamo and southern Quebrangulo inflows from the selected northern approach. The eastward river occupies the same mapped valley sequence as the selected line.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Capela junction and Atalaia–Sapucaia lower river
correspondence.finding: The Arapiraca original distinguishes the Paraibinha entering near Capela from the selected Paraíba arriving from Cajueiro. The Paraíba then turns south through Atalaia and Sapucaia and continues along the western approach to Pilar. The separately mapped Sumaúma-Mirim and other side channels are not substituted for the selected main course.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Pilar deltaic entrance and Lagoa Manguaba
correspondence.finding: The overlapping Arapiraca and Maceió originals establish the lower Paraíba approach, its branches southwest of Pilar, and entrance to the northwestern part of Lagoa Manguaba. The selected line crosses Manguaba southward, passing east of Marechal Deodoro. Maceió separately labels the Salgado approach and Sumaúma entering farther south/west; the neighboring Lagoa Mundaú and its inflow are separate. The municipal plan independently uses Rio Paraíba do Meio for the river with its mouth in Pilar.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Southern Manguaba outlet channels and terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The Maceió original shows the southern Manguaba exit entering the island/channel network around Massagueira, Santa Rita and Barra Nova. These channels connect northeastward to the Atlantic inlet alongside the southern Mundaú outlet system. This is the selected terminal coastal-channel setting. The model endpoint is treated at ordinary outlet-corridor scale: no claim is made that it is the surveyed open-ocean mouth, a separate inlet, or an exact match to a dated barrier edge. No single river hydronym is imposed on the lagoon or every coastal channel.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Unnamed western headward watercourse
correspondence.finding: The selected western start follows an irregular eastward watercourse through the small-waterbody landscape west and southwest of Owl Lake. The original sheet shows its southern excursion and return toward the outflow from Owl Lake. It is a separate branch from Fly Lake and Owl Lake; those northern lakes are not on this selected feeder.
correspondence.correspondence: Headward corridor and connection supported at ordinary generalized component scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Headward feeder name remains null. Do not assign Owl River, Fly Lake or Owl Lake as a uniform name to this component.

correspondence.component_scope: Junction below Owl Lake and upper Owl southern bend
correspondence.finding: The mapped Owl Lake outlet meets the western feeder south of the lake. The shared route bends southeast and then northeast, with the Owl label on the downstream watercourse. The large southern bend in the retained selected route corresponds to this mapped shared trunk rather than a passage through either named lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Junction and downstream bend supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Owl River applies to the shared mapped trunk; it does not rename the western feeder or the upstream lakes.

correspondence.component_scope: Herchmer and adjoining eastward trunk
correspondence.finding: The route turns north and then generally east/northeast through the Herchmer railway-crossing setting. The Herchmer sheet and provincial regional map place the Owl River at this crossing and show its continuation toward the park. Artuso's first-person 2011 field account independently describes paddling from Herchmer along Owl River to the Hudson Bay coast; this prose corroborates the route, without substituting for map coverage.
correspondence.correspondence: Overlapping mapped corridor and railway setting supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Owl River trunk; settlement and railway names are orientation only.

correspondence.component_scope: Central Owl River through Wapusk National Park
correspondence.finding: The original provincial and park maps follow the northeast-running Owl corridor through the park south of Broad River. Separate southern tributary channels remain distinct; the park map explicitly depicts Silcox Creek entering Owl River from the south. Skidmore Lake is north of the selected trunk and Roberge Lake is south of it, rather than selected lake passages. Continuous mapped trunk coverage bridges the Herchmer sheet's eastern edge to the coastal section.
correspondence.correspondence: Continuous central corridor and material tributary setting supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Representative Owl River name is supported by labels placed on the trunk, not merely by park or basin membership. Tributaries and off-route lakes retain separate scope.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Owl River and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: Both original maps continue the labeled Owl River to its own Hudson Bay outlet. The Parks Canada map places an Owl River management compound near the coast and depicts tidal flats along this shore. The river's outlet is distinct from the Broad River outlet to the north and Rupert Creek farther south. The selected lower east/northeast corridor reaches this same coastal setting.
correspondence.correspondence: Lower corridor, distinct outlet and receiving sea supported at ordinary mouth-area scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Hudson Bay is the receiving water, not an additional reach named Owl River. Exact shoreline or mouth-vertex identity is not asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Western head and Ramos Otero approach
correspondence.finding: The head lies in the El Yatay/Los Corrales country north of the separately mapped Arroyo Grande. The route proceeds northeast through the Ramos Otero setting toward Las Tres Lomas. The 1:100,000 original distinguishes Arroyo Grande and its southern tributaries from the Napaleofú drainage to the north. It does not show the selected intervening head-to-receiver link as a connected watercourse.
correspondence.correspondence: Original cartographic landscape read; hydrological connector materially unresolved.

correspondence.component_scope: Las Tres Lomas–El Refugio–La Oración–General Pirán lowland passage
correspondence.finding: The selected course turns east near El Refugio and San Pastor, then northeast through the La Oración/La Media Luna setting and crosses the transport corridor south of General Pirán. The detailed original shows discontinuous wetland/short-channel features in this country; the named Arroyo Chico is a distinct mapped corridor farther north before its eastern channelized connections. DiPAC describes intermittent streams, shallow basins and wet-period temporary connections, with paired imagery about 10 km west of General Pirán. Those regional observations do not identify the particular western selected receiving link.
correspondence.correspondence: Original geographic coverage and independently observed regional drainage character; not complete selected-connector correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern canal and Laguna del Maestro drainage setting
correspondence.finding: East of General Pirán, the selected route approaches the mapped Canal 6 and adjacent wetland country near San José de Mata and San Felipe, then the Cati Lauquén/La Paz depression-and-lagoon setting. The original 1:250,000 map shows Laguna del Maestro and its southeastern drainage. Glok Galli and DiPAC identify the natural Chico–Méndez drainage feeding the Maestro/La Argentina lake system and distinguish it from the canal network. The selected broad lagoon-to-coastal-channel passage is geographically consistent with this eastern receiving system; exact lake-edge and individual ditch positions are unassigned.
correspondence.correspondence: Original eastern corridor and lagoon drainage read; no back-propagation of names into the unresolved western head.

correspondence.component_scope: Cañada del Arroyo Chico / Chico o de las Gallinas and Canal 5 junction
correspondence.finding: The eastern selected route turns south and then southwest beside the coastal dune belt, through the Arroyo Chico/La Diana/Atlántida/Los Médanos country. The IGN original labels the lower natural drainage Arroyo Chico o de las Gallinas. The thesis's Figure 6.1 explicitly distinguishes the curved eastern Cañada del Arroyo Chico from the straighter Canal 5 approach farther west and shows their convergence before Laguna Mar Chiquita. Its prose describes the cañada as the outlet drainage of La Argentina and El Maestro. This supplies the material lower receiving junction; the canal and natural cañada are not treated as one uniformly named channel.
correspondence.correspondence: Original mapped lower channel and material receiving connection, corroborated by bounded prose.
mapped_component_names: Arroyo Chico o de las Gallinas

correspondence.component_scope: Laguna Mar Chiquita passage and neighboring lakes
correspondence.finding: The selected route continues southwest into the northern part of Laguna Mar Chiquita and traverses its main coastal-lagoon body. Original maps distinguish nearby Hinojales, Nahuel Rucá and other western lagoons rather than placing all of them on the selected passage. Glok Galli's basin figure independently shows the lagoon receiving the eastern cañada/canal system and other separately named western tributaries. No reservoir or dam passage is shown in the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: Original lagoon and receiving-basin cartography, with generalized interior passage only.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern lagoon inlet and actual Atlantic terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected terminal follows the lagoon's narrowing southern inlet beside the Mar Chiquita settlement and opens through the coastal barrier to the Atlantic. The IGN original shows the lagoon, constricted outlet, settlement and sea together; the thesis independently describes the lagoon's sea-communication channel and maps that connection. The endpoint is this open coastal outlet, not an inland termination or one of the neighboring lakes. Offshore white patches in the detailed mosaic do not intersect the terminal passage and are not used as evidence.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal setting and lagoon-to-sea connection read on original cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Extreme southeastern selected headward beginning
correspondence.finding: The selected beginning lies in the uplands across the Río Negro–Chubut boundary. Original 250k topography was read at overview and detailed scale: the downstream part reaches a mapped intermittent feeder, while the extreme beginning lies beyond the depicted blue-channel network. The 100k extent is entirely white. DPA's broad headwater account and basin figure cannot supply the specific missing linkage.
correspondence.correspondence: Material connection unresolved.
correspondence.name_scope: Do not assign Maquinchao or a nearby upland name to this unresolved initial feeder.

correspondence.component_scope: Established feeder and Llama-Niyeo–Rucu-Luan transition
correspondence.finding: Downstream of the unresolved extreme beginning, the selected route corresponds to the mapped intermittent drainage toward Llama-Niyeo and its northward turn into the broader Rucu-Luan valley setting. Several western and eastern feeder valleys are visible. These junctions were read geographically, rather than treating a nearby place label as the river name.
correspondence.correspondence: Established downstream feeder and valley junctions supported at ordinary corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: No separate headward feeder hydronym established.

correspondence.component_scope: Puesto de Hornos–Renangueyeu–Ñe-Luan middle corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected route follows the long north-running channel and mallín belt through the Puesto de Hornos and Renangueyeu settings toward Ñe-Luan. Original cartography places the Río Maquinchao label along the continuing trunk. Ñe-Luan and other lagoons lie beside or within neighboring branches of this wetland landscape; the selected route is not a continuous traverse of their open-water interiors. DPA separately identifies a secondary Maquinchao arm feeding Ñe-Luan.
correspondence.correspondence: Middle channel, wetland and branch setting supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Maquinchao supports the trunk candidate, without renaming neighboring lakes or all side channels.

correspondence.component_scope: Maquinchao bend and west-running lower trunk
correspondence.finding: Original cartography follows the selected course past Estancia Maquinchao and the railway setting into its westward turn near Maquinchao and Cerro Puntudo, then along the Epu Laufquen lowland north of the main road/rail corridor. Repeated Río Maquinchao labeling lies on the same mapped drainage. Southern tributary valleys enter this low belt; DPA and SEGEMAR independently distinguish Chaiful and Quetrequile, with SEGEMAR also describing Pistola.
correspondence.correspondence: Named lower trunk, direction change and material tributary setting supported.
correspondence.name_scope: The tributaries remain distinct and are not included in a uniform Maquinchao scalar claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower wetland convergence and Cari Laufquen Chica setting
correspondence.finding: The west-running selected line enters the low channel/mallín convergence south and east of Cari Laufquen Chica. DPA describes Maquinchao and Huahuel Niyeo joining north of RN23 before the lake. The original map shows their convergent watercourse setting. The model skirts the east side of Chica rather than matching its mapped open-water centre; no exact bank or artificial lake-interior river name is asserted.
correspondence.correspondence: Generalized convergence, lake-margin and outlet approach supported.
correspondence.name_scope: Cari Laufquen Chica remains a distinct lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Chica outlet, Cerro Ambrosio and actual Grande terminal
correspondence.finding: The detailed original terminal map shows an intermittent outlet leaving the north/east side of Chica, bending around the east side of Cerro Ambrosio and then northwest into Grande. The selected generalized continuation follows this outlet corridor and finishes within mapped Laguna Cari Laufquen Grande. SEGEMAR describes the temporary lower-Maquinchao connection between the lakes, corroborating DPA's outlet account.
correspondence.correspondence: Lake connector and endorheic receiving-water setting supported at ordinary corridor scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Maquinchao is the linked river-system candidate; lake interiors retain their lake identities.
